record.paper_title: Some Open Questions about Symplectic 4-Manifolds, Singular Plane Curves, and Braid Group Factorizations
record.original_question: Let D_1 and D_2 be symplectic plane curves in CP^2 with only positive nodes and cusps, having the same degree and the same numbers of nodes and cusps. Determine whether D_2 can always be obtained from D_1 by a finite sequence of braiding operations along embedded Lagrangian annuli in the complement, where such a braiding replaces two parallel local branches near the annulus boundary by a half-twisted configuration and corresponds on the branched cover side to Luttinger surgery.

evidence.quote: Question 3.17. Let D1, D2 be two symplectic curves with positive nodes and cusps in CP^2, of the same degree and with the same numbers of nodes and cusps. Is it always possible to obtain D2 from D1 by a sequence of braiding operations along Lagrangian annuli?
This construction is called “braiding” because, forgetting the S^1 factor, it replaces the trivial braid (−1, 1) × {±1/2} with the half-twist Γ̃.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{CP}^2$ equipped with its standard Fubini–Study symplectic form. A symplectic plane curve is a (possibly singular) 2-dimensional subset $D \subset \mathbb{CP}^2$ that is a smooth symplectic submanifold away from finitely many singular points, each of which is locally modeled on a positive node (transverse intersection of two smooth symplectic branches with positive intersection number) or a positive cusp (locally modeled on $\{z_1^2 = z_2^3\}$ in suitable symplectic coordinates).

Two such curves $D_1$ and $D_2$ are said to have the same combinatorial type if they have the same degree, the same number of nodes, and the same number of cusps.

A braiding operation along an embedded Lagrangian annulus is defined as follows. Suppose $A \subset \mathbb{CP}^2 \setminus D$ is an embedded Lagrangian annulus whose two boundary circles lie on $D$, each parallel to a local symplectic branch of $D$. In a Weinstein neighborhood of $A$, identified with $T^*A$, the curve $D$ locally consists of two parallel sheets near $\partial A$; the braiding operation cuts out a neighborhood of these two parallel sheets and reglues them as a half-twisted band (replacing the trivial braid $(-1,1) \times \{\pm 1/2\}$, viewed in $A \times (-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ modulo the $S^1$-factor, by a half-twist $\widetilde{\Gamma}$), producing a new symplectic curve with the same combinatorial type. On the double (or branched) cover this operation corresponds to a Luttinger surgery along an embedded Lagrangian torus.

Question: Given any two symplectic plane curves $D_1, D_2 \subset \mathbb{CP}^2$ with only positive nodes and cusps and with the same combinatorial type, must $D_2$ always be obtainable from $D_1$ by a finite sequence of braiding operations along embedded Lagrangian annuli?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as Question 3.17 in Auroux's list of open questions on symplectic 4-manifolds and singular plane curves. No subsequent work resolving it in general has been located; later surveys by Auroux continue to list it among open isotopy/braiding problems, and known partial results address only specific families of examples via Luttinger surgery on branched covers.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic 4-manifolds, singular plane curves, and isotopy problems
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent survey by Auroux still discussing braiding along Lagrangian annuli as a tool relating non-isotopic singular plane curves, without claiming a general answer.
